papers.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
papers.abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(\Omega(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.

papers.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.

papers.title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
papers.abstract: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.

papers.title: Associated primes in group cohomology and a strange result
papers.abstract: In 2010. Okuyama proved the following. Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ dividing the order of $G$. (1) Let $\frak p$ be an associated prime of $H^*(G,k)$ of $\dim=s$. Then there exists an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup $E\subseteq G$ of rank $s$ with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_E$ and depth$\,H^*(C_GE,k)=s$. (2) Let $E$ be an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ of rank $s$ and suppose depth$\,H^*(C_GE,k)=s$. Then $\mathfrak p_E$ is an associated prime of $H^*(G,k)$. It is shown this result is true for all fields of characteristic $p$. We also show the following result: If $E$ is an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ and depth $H^*(G,k)=\text{rank} E$, then up to conjugation $E$ contains the maximal elementary abelian subgroup contained in the center of a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$.

papers.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar Groups
papers.abstract: We study the singular loci of the reduced $\SL_2(\CC)$-representation varieties $R_{m,n}$ of non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar groups $B(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid b^{-1}a^m b=a^n\rangle$. We determine their dimensions and profile functions, which list the numbers of irreducible components in descending order of dimension. The components have dimensions three or five. Their reduced singular loci have the explicit description \[ \Sing R_{m,n} =\left\{(\varepsilon I,Y): \varepsilon^m=\varepsilon^n,\quad (\tr Y)^2=\frac{(m+n)^2}{mn}\right\}, \] where $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ and $Y\in\SL_2(\CC)$. Each is a disjoint union of $\mu$ copies of the smooth affine quadric $Q=\{(x,y,z)\in\CC^3:x^2+yz=1\}$, where $\mu=2$ for $m-n$ odd and $\mu=4$ for $m-n$ even. Thus its complex algebraic isomorphism type depends only on this parity. Each quadric is homotopy equivalent to $S^2$, so the singular locus has integral homology $\ZZ^\mu$ in degrees zero and two and zero in all other degrees. An algebraic stratification gives its compactly supported E-polynomial $\mu(q^2+q)$, with $q=uv$. At every singular point, $R_{m,n}$ is locally analytically the product of a smooth surface and a nodal curve.

papers.title: Infinite Girth, Finite Quotients, and Nielsen Connectivity in Groups
papers.abstract: We develop new methods for studying infinite girth in finitely generated residually finite groups, particularly those containing no non-abelian free subgroups and satisfying no non-trivial group law. Our main contribution is a probabilistic Nielsen-component lifting principle, based on product replacement graphs, which provides a criterion for transferring suitable generation and word-avoidance properties of finite quotients to the ambient group. As an application, we prove that every finitely generated group admitting infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic non-abelian finite simple quotients has infinite girth, with extensions to quasisimple and, under additional hypotheses, almost-simple quotients. We further establish infinite girth for the B. H. Neumann group and the Bou-Rabee-Seward group, obtaining new results on the occurrence of non-abelian finite simple quotients and sections. By a different construction, we also prove that Alt_fin(Z) semidirect Z has infinite girth. Finally, we establish a marked finite-quotient characterization of infinite girth for finitely generated residually finite groups and prove that, for linear groups over fields of characteristic zero, large marked girth can be realized in congruence quotients. We conclude with several open questions and remarks arising from our results.

papers.title: Diagram of Geodesic Intervals in $C'(1/8)$-Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a group characterized by a small cancellation $C'(1/8)$-presentation. We study the structure of its Cayley graph, specifically geodesic intervals and digons. We prove that all geodesic segments $[x,y]$ of length $n$ can be covered by finitely many simple geodesic digons with pairwise $C'(1/8)$-short lower intersections whose lower sides lie on a common geodesic segment $[x,y]$. This is a generalization of a proposition of Kharlampovich-Sklinos (arXiv:2106.05461) for random groups. We then bound this resulting diagram of digons, showing that the total perimeter of its cells and its edge count is bounded by $n$, and the cycle rank is equal to the number of distinct cell contours. Thus, although there may be many different geodesics, the size of their union is bounded linearly in the distance between their endpoints. The constant is independent of the number and lengths of the defining relators. In particular, the estimate applies to infinite presentations with unbounded relator lengths. From this we get a consequence for growth, allowing us to compare the number of geodesic words with the number of group elements of the same length.

papers.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
papers.abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.

papers.title: Spectral Fields and Unitary Descent: Local splitting, simultaneous norms, and transcendental obstructions
papers.abstract: Spectral fields can recover matrix coefficients without standardizing the invariant Hermitian form. Over an algebraic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ stable under nontrivial complex conjugation, we prove that every Zariski-dense subgroup in a normalized Hermitian model of dimension $m\ge4$ and signature $(m-1,1)$ at the fixed embedding contains a loxodromic element whose spectrum makes all diagonal coefficients norms. The element can be chosen so that every positive power is regular and generates the same splitting field. For an arbitrary initial Hermitian model over such a field, two spectra suffice for standard unitary descent over an extension of relative degree at most $(m!)^2$. Over every quadratic extension $F/k$ of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero, a four-dimensional quasi-split unitary group of Witt index two contains a discrete, Zariski-dense free subgroup whose spectra all split over $F$. Over intrinsic fields of positive transcendence degree, we construct a single convex cocompact, Zariski-dense free subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(3,1)$ for which, for every initial regular element and every normalized extraction, the Hermitian obstruction persists after adjoining any finite family of spectra and over the total spectral field.

papers.title: On subgroup perfect codes and regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: A subset $C$ of the vertex set of a graph $\Gamma$ is said to be an $(a,b)$-regular set if $C$ induces an $a$-regular subgraph and every vertex outside $C$ is adjacent to exactly $b$ vertices in $C$. A $(0,1)$-regular set is called a perfect code. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ be such that $\alpha^2=\mathrm{id}$. Let $\omega_\alpha(G)=\{\alpha(g^{-1})g:g\in G\}$. For a subset $S\subseteq G$ satisfying $\alpha(S)=S^{-1}$ and $S\cap\omega_\alpha(G)=\emptyset$, the generalized Cayley graph of $(G,\alpha)$ with respect to $S$ is the graph with vertex set $G$ in which two distinct elements $g,h\in G$ are adjacent if and only if $\alpha(g^{-1})h\in S$. In this paper, we prove two main results. First, let $H$ be an $\alpha$-invariant subgroup of a finite group $G$, and let $P$ be an $\alpha$-invariant Sylow 2-subgroup of $H$. We show that $H$ is a perfect code of $(G,\alpha)$ if and only if $P[H,\alpha]$ is a perfect code of $(G,\alpha)$, where $[H,\alpha]=\langle h^{-1}\alpha(h):h\in H\rangle$. Second, we consider finite groups $G$ possessing a cyclic subgroup $A$ of index 2 that is invariant under an involutory automorphism $\alpha$. We show that $\omega_\alpha(G)$ is a subgroup of $A$. Using this result, we give a complete characterization of all pairs $(a,b)$ for which an $\alpha$-invariant subgroup $H$ of $G$ is an $(a,b)$-regular set of $(G,\alpha)$. In particular, our characterization applies to all finite groups possessing a characteristic cyclic subgroup of index 2, for every involutory automorphism $\alpha$.

papers.title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: Let $p>3$ and let $\Gamma$ be a non-elementary Gromov hyperbolic group with $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. We prove that every $\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$-convex cocompact representation $$ \rho:\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PO}_{p,3} $$ whose proximal limit set $\Lambda_\rho\subset\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$ is a $C^1$ submanifold preserves a totally geodesic copy of $\mathbb{H}^p\subset\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$. Consequently, $\Gamma/\ker \rho$ is virtually a cocompact lattice in $\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^p)$. For odd $p$, we prove the same conclusion for every signature $(p,q)$ with $p>q\ge2$, under the same hypothesis $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. Our methods combine dynamics, differential topology, and representation theory. The key new ingredient is to study the radicals of the semidefinite forms induced on the tangent spaces of the limit set. They form a continuous vector bundle of constant rank. The tangent action at attracting fixed points gives a bound, in terms of the radical rank, on the number of eigenvalues of an orthogonal lift whose modulus exceeds one. We then use the topology of the sphere and the representation theory of real algebraic groups to exclude the remaining possibilities. In arbitrary signature with $p>q$, these arguments already imply that a representation with a $C^1$ limit set cannot be Zariski dense.

papers.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
papers.abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: Buildings governed by twisted Bruhat orders
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a twisted building associated to a Coxeter system and an initial section of a reflection order. These are pairs of buildings and a map between them which depends on a twisted Bruhat order. It is proved that projection maps exist between components and that the common apartment property holds for a suitable notion of an apartment, generalising what is known for twin buildings. Several well-known examples are given, including a family of twisted buildings associated to an affine building and its fa\c{c}ades.

papers.title: A complete description of the algebraic structure of pseudocompact abelian groups
papers.abstract: We solve a major open problem from [D. Dikranjan, D. Shakhmatov, Algebraic structure of pseudocompact groups, Memoirs AMS 633 (1998)] by describing abelian groups which admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. First, we prove that an abelian group G can be equipped with a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology iff it can be decomposed into a direct sum G=B\oplus H of a bounded torsion group B and agroup H satisfying |nH|=|H| for all positive integers $n$, such that both B and H admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. Second, for an unbounded abelian group G, we denote by m the minimal positive integer n such that |nG|=|kG| for all integers k\ge n. Then G admits a pseudocompact group topology iff both G[m]={g\in G: mg=0} and mG\cong G/G[m] admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology.

papers.title: Finite groups with all involutions fused
papers.abstract: We characterize finite groups whose involutions form a single fusion class. In the solvable case, we show that the $2$-length is $1$, extending Thompson's theorem which states that a solvable group with all involutions conjugate has $2$-length $1$. For a nonsolvable group $G$, we prove that if its involutions are fused then they are conjugate; moreover, $G/\mathbf{O}_{2'}(G)$ is almost quasisimple. As an application, we obtain a restriction on $m$ for which an $m$-pyramidal Kirkman triple system can be realized under a nonsolvable group.

papers.title: Centralizers of maps as automorphism groups of Yang--Baxter solutions
papers.abstract: For a partition $X = Y \sqcup Z$ of a set $X$ and an arbitrary map $g \colon Y \to {\rm Hom}_{\rm Set} (Z, \, Z)$, we construct a solution $R_g \colon X \times X \to X \times X$ of the braid equation. We characterize intrinsically the solutions which are isomorphic to some $R_g$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for two solutions $R_g$ and $R_{g'}$ to be isomorphic. Consequently, the number of isomorphism classes of the solutions $R_g$ on a set with $n$ elements is $1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{n-1} \widetilde{o} (n - k, \, k)$, where $\widetilde{o} (m, \, k)$ is the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$, acting by conjugation, on the set of multisets with $k$ elements of maps $\{1, \ldots, m\} \to \{1, \ldots, m\}$. This construction is then used to obtain a solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is exactly the centralizer ${\rm Aut} (f_1, \ldots, f_k)$ of a given family $f_1, \ldots, f_k \colon X \to X$ of maps, $k \geq 1$. For $k = 2$, combined with a result of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, this gives another proof of the fact that any group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a solution of the braid equation (equivalently, of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation).

papers.title: Catalan Semirings
papers.abstract: We study Catalan semirings, which are additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups belong to a natural family of transformation monoids known as Catalan monoids. There are two kinds of Catalan semirings, whose properties differ substantially. We address the Finite Basis Problem for individual Catalan semirings of each kind and their representations by Boolean triangular matrices. Furthermore, we characterize the varieties and pseudovarieties generated by all Catalan semirings of each kind.

papers.title: Cost of one-relator groups
papers.abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $\Gamma=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $\beta^{(2)}_1(\Gamma)=\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.

papers.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
papers.abstract: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.

papers.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. More unexpectedly, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite groups, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

papers.title: The Exact Central-Index Profile of Groups with Bounded Noncommutativity
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, let $\omega(G)$ be the largest size of a pairwise noncommuting set and put $z(G)=[G:\mathrm Z(G)]$. We determine the maximum possible central index under $\omega(G)\le k$ for every integer $k\ge1$, giving an exact answer to Neumann's central-index question and sharpening Pyber's exponential upper bound. The maximum is $1$ for $k=1,2$, $(k-1)^2$ for $3\le k\le6$, $81$ for $k=7,8$, and $4^{\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor}$ for $k\ge9$. In the last range, with $r=\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor$, equality holds exactly when $G'\cong C_2$ and $G/\mathrm Z(G)\cong\mathbb F_2^{2r}$. We also obtain the sharp universal bound $z(G)\le(81/64)2^{\omega(G)-1}$. All maximizers are classified up to isoclinism. The results extend to arbitrary groups with finite clique number through finite isoclinic representatives.

papers.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $\pi_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2\pi/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle \tau\rangle$, where $\tau$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.

papers.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
papers.abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

papers.title: Chain Conditions for Abelian Normal Subgroups
papers.abstract: We investigate various chain conditions for abelian normal subgroups of groups, following Robinson (1968). We focus on the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups, an exceptional case excluded from his results except for some counterexamples. In particular we show that a hypercentral group satisfies the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups if and only if it is is finitely generated nilpotent.

papers.title: $M$-subgroups and normal-subgroup lattices of finite groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group. A normal subgroup $E$ is an $M$-subgroup if $E\cap N_1\cap N_2\neq1$ whenever $N_1\cap N_2$, $E\cap N_1$, and $E\cap N_2$ are non-trivial for normal subgroups $N_1,N_2$. We characterise these subgroups as the essential or relatively uniform normal subgroups. For finite $G$, an $M$-subgroup is either trivial, contains exactly one minimal normal subgroup, or contains the socle. Consequently, every normal subgroup is an $M$-subgroup precisely when the socle has $G$-chief length at most two. We obtain an explicit $M$-closure operation and describe the minimal normal subgroups of finite direct products. For crown-based powers, we use the known comparability of normal subgroups with the socle to describe the normal lattice in terms of Boolean or subspace lattices and the quotient above the socle. We then determine when the $M$-lattice retains the normal lattice, classify normal quotients and their automorphism orbits, and characterise quotient maps compatible with $M$-closure. Finally, we compute the maximal length of chains of $M$-subgroups in terms of the chief length and socle length of $G$.

papers.title: Finite Groups with Few Almost Maximal Subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group. L. Morgana, C. E. Praeger, A.E. Zalesski \cite {MOR} introduced the notion of almost maximal subgroup of $G$. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be almost maximal in $G$ if $N_G(H)$ is maximal in $G$. In this paper, let $AM(G)$ denote the number of conjugacy classes of all almost maximal subgroups of $G$. First, we prove that $G$ is Dedekindian if and only if $AM(G)=0$. Second, we show that the finite groups with $AM(G)\leq 1$ are supersolvable. Furthermore, we characterize the structure of finite groups with $AM(G)=1$. Final, we investigate a lower bound of $AM(G)$ for certain non-solvable groups.

papers.title: On a finite group in which every maximal subgroup of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is nilpotent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ any fixed prime divisor of $|G|$. We prove that if every maximal subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is nilpotent then $G$ is a solvable group having a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.

papers.title: A note on an extension of Shidov's theorem and Shlyk's theorem
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-solvable group and $p$ any fixed prime divisor of $|G|$. We prove that the intersection of all non-nilpotent maximal subgroups of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is $p$-closed, which provides a further generalization of Shidov's theorem and Shlyk's theorem.

papers.title: Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $\omega$ be a smooth positive density, and let $\mu$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms. For $g\ge2$ and quasimorphisms vanishing on the disc braid group, we obtain an injective map to $C^0$-continuous homogeneous quasimorphisms on $Homeo_0(N_g,\mu)$. We also obtain undistortion criteria in $Homeo_0(N_g)$ and $Diff_0(N_g)$. For $g=1,2$ and every $d\ge2$, we prove $$ \dim\overline H_b^d(Homeo_0(N_g,\mu))=\infty,\qquad \dim\overline{EH}_b^d(Diff_0(N_g,\omega))=\infty. $$ Moreover, $\overline{EH}_b^d(Homeo_0(N_2,\mu))$ is infinite dimensional in every positive even degree $d$. Here $\overline{H}_b^d$ and $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denote reduced bounded cohomology and reduced exact bounded cohomology, respectively.

papers.title: Digital Finite Group Theory
papers.abstract: This book develops a digital formulation of finite group theory, in which every finite group of order $N$ is represented as the alphabet $\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$ endowed with the transported group product. Multiplication, inversion and related structure are written explicitly as integer operations on labels. The foundations treat digit functions, codes of permutations and $r$-ary operators, finite magmas, and constructions of laws from diagrams. Classical parts of finite group theory, including conjugacy classes, stabiliser chains and characters, are recast as identities between digits of codes. The book gives explicit digital laws for all groups of order at most 32, the finite quotients of the 17 plane and 230 space crystallographic groups, the symmetric and alternating groups, the finite simple groups of Lie type, and all 26 sporadic groups. For most sporadic groups the laws are obtained by chain constructions; for the Baby Monster and the Monster they are computed structurally from the 196884-dimensional representation and evaluated with the mmgroup package. The accompanying software archive reproduces the laws, tables and worked examples as verifiable integer data.
